news.title: India end FIFA U15 World Cup Festival campaign with 6-4 win over Cuba
news.lede: Baku (Azerbaijan): India boys concluded their campaign on a winning note at the FIFA U15 World Cup and Festival, defeating Cuba 6-4 in the 87th-place play-off at the Hovsan Competition Complex Pitch 1B in Baku, Azerbaijan, on Friday. Victor Lalawmpuia, Nibas Meetei Wahengbam and R Lalremruatfela scored twice each as the Blue Colts secured victory in their 10th and final fixture of the tournament. India built a commanding 6-1 lead before Cuba scored three late goals to narrow the margin. At the inaugural FIFA U15 World Cup and Festival, India registered five wins, against Laos, Cameroon, Bahrain, Trinidad and Tobago, and Cuba.

news.title: England U15s stars PROTECT referee during World Cup brawl vs Bolivia just days after alleged racist incident
news.lede: ENGLAND Under-15s jumped in to protect a referee during a World Cup and Festival match against Bolivia. At the very end of the match, the Young Lions were awarded what was deemed to be a controversial penalty. But as the No11 stepped up to take it, the Bolivia goalkeeper moved over to the left side and refused to attempt the save. The England star was then able to pass the ball into the empty net to give the nation a 3-2 lead.

news.title: Fifa to miss equal Women’s World Cup prize money ambition set by Infantino
news.lede: Infantino said in 2023 equality was Fifa’s target. Prize money could double but big gap will remain. Fifa is to fall short of gender equality with the prize money on offer at next year’s Women’s World Cup, despite making a record $15bn (£11.2bn) in revenue from this summer’s men’s tournament. Gianni Infantino, the Fifa president, said in 2023 that the organisation’s ambition was to have equality for the prize pot for 2027, saying: “Fifa is stepping up with actions, not just with words.”

news.title: PH 110th of 189 nations in 2026 FIFA U15 World Cup
news.lede: BAKU – The Philippine Under-15 Men’s National Football Team (PMNFT U15) concluded its maiden FIFA World Cup & Festival at a respectable 110th place out of 189 countries in the world’s biggest football tournament in terms of participation here. This came after a dramatic final match between the Philippines and Andorra, with the European side winning, 2-1 off a late goal. It was an exchange of goals in the opening two minutes, with Andorra’s Max Rossell scoring an Olimpico from the left corner kick 23 seconds in, but Filipino winger Sylar Alcantara respondent a minute later with a long shot from midfield to tie the game. PMNFT U15 had the more dangerous chances on goal but Andorran goalkeeper Joan Caballol was a tough nut to crack between the sticks.
